utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We must apologise that an urgent matter caused a delay and we have kept you waiting. Could the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, before the witness is brought in, can I ask you very briefly for your indulgence to inform you in two minutes in connection with your recommendation at the end of our session yesterday. The defence of General Strugar is totally open for all conversation along the lines that you suggested, and the suggestion that you recommended. As far as I could understand, my learned colleague Mr. Kaufman, the opposite side, is at this time not ready to give up the concept and the manner of presentation of their evidence at this point of time so that unfortunately, despite the best of will on our part, I have to proceed in the same way as I did yesterday and will have to do so in the case of some future witnesses. Otherwise, it is always to discuss this matter in the way that you suggested. And I would also be so free to suggest that perhaps we could organise a sort of a 65 ter conference. And with your assistance and help, perhaps we could discuss this in detail so you could see what it is that we are suggesting and what argumentation we wish to present along those lines. Perhaps in a different setting this would be more convenient, of course, if there is a similar wish on the other side. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm grateful for your indication, Mr. Petrovic. Thank you. Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes. If I just make comment, Your Honours. It is correct that there is an open channel of communication. It is also correct that at the conclusion of yesterday's hearing that Mr. Petrovic and I did have a conversation on how best to deal with the matters that were raised by Your Honours at the end of the last hearing. I am mindful of Your Honours' direction, and I am not precluding at this point in time that at a later date we might in any event reach an agreement as to the extent of the damage. However, at this moment in time, the Prosecution is not able to relinquish Annex 2 to the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that carry with it the view that some meeting, as suggested by Mr. Petrovic, would not be productive?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I believe that a meeting would be productive. I believe, furthermore, as Ms. Somers herself has stated in a previous hearing that a suggested 65 ter conference would be acceptable to the Prosecution as well, of course. So if the Trial Chamber is minded to hold such a conference at a later date, I'm sure it will enable both sides to reach agreements.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: How much later would that later date be, Mr. Kaufman?

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Obviously it would not be possible today, and obviously it would be advisable that the Senior Trial Attorney would be present at such a 65 ter conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The answer then is? Next week.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If Your Honours are minded to hold such a conference next week, of course the Prosecution would be willing to hold such a conference at such a date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kaufman. We'll leave the matter at that point, then, and we'll give some consideration to it at a later time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see that Dr. Kaiser has come into the Court and has presumed his seat. May we apologise to you as well that an urgent matter caused a delay in the starting time and has kept you waiting, and I'm afraid, as you've probably picked up, you must experience more of the process that was under way yesterday today. Yes, Mr. Petrovic. If I could remind you of the affirmation you took at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Kaiser.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can at the beginning all these documents be presented to the witness, all these relevant documents, E51 and B62, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kaiser, will you first of all, please, look at the document which constitutes the preliminary report, which is P51, the first page of the first binder. This is the document L0061411 in the English translation. Do you have that document before you, Mr. Kaiser?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree with me that the title of this report is the preliminary report on the damage inflicted on the old core of the city of Dubrovnik in October, November, and December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Will you now please look at page -- in the English version is the L0061412. That is the next page in the English version, the same document. On the top of the page we again have the title of the report; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the title.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then the authors of the report are indicated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The authors are Marko Vetma, Franic Popic, and Vukovic; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you kindly now move on to page L0061414 in the English translation. Do you see this page?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this the -- are these the introductory remarks to the preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: They appear to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, then, that on the next page you can see the signature? Please take a look. Is it correct that the date which the report bears is the 6th of January, 1992? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And also, is it correct that the introduction to the preliminary report is signed by the director of the institute, i.e., the Institute for the Protection of Monuments of Culture and Nature, Mrs. Dorotea Valjalo?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see her name written down there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the next page. This page describes the methods which were employed. Please pay attention to the second paragraph on that page. Is it written there -- is there a reference there, rather, to the time when the Old Town of Dubrovnik was bombarded and an indication of the dates of the 24th and the 25th of November and the 6th of December and a number of dates in October?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the dates written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Are these the dates to which this preliminary report refers?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the dates of which it purports to refer to, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the part of the preliminary report which deals with damage to the ramparts. The mark is Z21. And that is, Your Honours, in translation L0061443. Have you found it, Mr. Kaiser?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found Z21.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the 24th of November, 1991, is the date which is the date which is indicated as the impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date indicated there is indeed the 24th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Take a look at Z43 now, please. This is, Your Honours, L0061465. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So take a look at the date of the impact, of the alleged impact.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the dates are clear, the 12th of November and the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one minute, please. Take a look at what is at insula 548. The number is 600 -- L0048498. Insula 548.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at the date of the impact.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now take a look at, for instance -- take a look at, for instance, mark 9-3. It is L0059946 in the English translation. I assume it's in book number two. Have you found -- is it correct that the date of 13 December 1991 is indicated there as the date of the impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is. The 13th of December, 1991, is written down here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now please take a look at -- just bear with me for a second, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I rise to my feet at this point in time because, although I am conscious of what is written with respect to the last site, in the English translation I have asked my colleague Ms. Matacic to analyse the B/C/S version of the same site, and there it would appear that the date is 13.X1.1991 as the date of the hit, which would mean it was November. So I would beg Mr. Petrovic to be very careful when he's putting these questions to the witness that he is citing the date as it is in the B/C/S version, and he's not putting to the witness something which is in fact a mistake in the translation which has been provided by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I base myself on this translation as it is much easier for me to look at the B/C/S version and proceed in this way. If you wish me to change that, I can do that, but I'm doing it in this way in the interests of the Chamber. But in my learned colleague so wishes, I will gladly deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, from the point of the view of the Chamber, as you have indicated the English-language translation is far more useful. If there is some deficiency in the English-language translation, I would ask Mr. Kaufman to point it out as we go along. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at -- just one minute. I've lost it now. For instance, 13-2, which in the English version is L0048569. Have you found it? Does it indicate the 10th of November, 1991, as the date of the shelling, of the impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please, also immediately following, 13-4. Does it indicate the 27th of November, 1991, as the date of the impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it indicates the 27th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So I am not going to take any more of your time or the Chamber's time. So I've chosen several of these indications from the beginning, the middle, and the end of this preliminary report which are example which exemplify that this preliminary report should contain, should refer to damage inflicted in October, November, and December. So in this context, I should like to ask you the question whether you still stick to your statement which you rendered here yesterday, which is the that the preliminary report only refers to damages inflicted on the 6th of December, or do you accept that you made a mistake in so stating yesterday?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: We asked that they do a damage survey of the bombardment damage which was done on the 6th of December, and the reasons this was asked was because there existed -- although in notes at that time -- there was a report which I was preparing which was about the earlier damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please reply to my question. Is this a report which refers to October, November, and December; and is it correct in that context what you said yesterday, that the report contains only damage which was inflicted on the 6th of December, not what you asked them about or for but what the report contains, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that this report contains damage on the earlier period, but what I've said to you about the 6th of December and what the intention -- our intention was remains, remains so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What can you then say to me today about this report? Is this a report -- is, first of all, the title of this report correct at all?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from the title of the report and you can see from the content that there is damage from October, November, and December in their report, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So there is a correlation between the title of the report which is adequate to the content of the report, which is damage in October, November, and December. Is that not so?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you know, I have not examined this report from cover to cover, and I have not made any comparisons. The report says October, November, and December. I cannot assure you that all the damage of October and November would be in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look at your own report. Let's go back to Annex 3 of your report, which unfortunately, Your Honours, I still do not have in any of the languages which is usable by the Defence. I don't have it in either English or the B/C/S version. Please find Annex 3 to your report. Can you please give me the answer to this question: In your report which covers October and November damage, does it say under item 20, Dropceva Street number 2?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No translation. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Well, the translator translated. Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So under item 20, do you have Dropceva Street, number 2, in your report for October and November?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now take a look at the preliminary report, book 6-9. The first volume, the first book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, Your Honours, is L0061064.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I've found it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is the date indicated there the date of impact, that is, is it the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you now look in your report under item 21, Annex 3 to your report for October, November. So under item 21, please take a look at Zamanjina Street, number 1. Is it indicated in your report for October and November under item 23, Zamanjina Street, number 23 -- No, 21, sorry -- item 21 of your report for October and November?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 21 is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at the report of the institute, 6-1, L0061074. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is 6th of December, 1991, indicated there as the date of impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at item 22 of your report. That is Antuninska Street number 1, hit in October or November 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now look at the report of the institute, 7- -- sorry, just one minute. So it's 7-14, 0061092 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is the 6th of December, 1991, indicated there as the date of impact?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look now at your report, item 23. The street is called Izmedju Polaca 21, your report for October and November. Is it true the damage is in October, November, Izmedju Polaca street, number 24?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Number 24.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you now have a look at the institute's report, 8-38. In the English translation it's 0059915.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does it say that the date of the hit is the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at item 25 of your report for October and November. Siroka Street number 8. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you find in the preliminary report the damage you found in this report for October and November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you help me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you if you are able to find it yourself. If not, I'll tell I what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which insula it was contained in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is my assertion that in the preliminary report there is no information whatsoever on Siroka Street number 8. Do you accept my assertion?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I believe you if you say you can't find it in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at item 26 of your report. Siroka Street number 5, damage inflicted in October and November 1991. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at the preliminary report now. Insula 9-36.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. This seems to end at 9-25.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: My apologies. It's my mistake. Not 9-36. It's 11-36. I'm sorry. So it's 0061533.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does is say the 6th of December, 1991, is the date of the hit?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you now look at item 27. Which building is that, item 27 of your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the senior citizens' home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you find this building in the preliminary report of the institute for October, November, December 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It would be helpful if you would indicate the insula and eventually the report form number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I can't help you because it is not there in the report of the institute for October, November, December. Will you now look at item 30 of your report for October and November. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now have a look at insula 13, building number 5. In the English translation it's 0048572.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that building that you referenced in item 30 the St. Mary's Convent?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's referenced.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that in the preliminary report the date of the hit is indicated as the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the date is the 6th of December. It indicates other kinds of damage, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please look at item 32 of your report.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does it say Gucetica Street?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Damage indicated is October, November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now look at insula 11-1. In English it's 0061497. 11-1, that is, 1A.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I've found that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The date of the hit is the 6th of December, 1991; isn't it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Look at item 33 in your report. Your report on damage for October, November 1991, is there an indication of Strossmayerova Street number 5?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my report it is. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the report of the institute for October, November, and December, can you find this Strossmayerova Street, referencing damage in October, November, December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I'd like to ask you to help me again to find it by indicating which --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. It's not there. No such damage is recorded in the report for the institute for October, November, December. Look at item 4 of your report. Sigurata Monastery. Sigurata Monastery. Have you located it in your report? You're looking at your report; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You've got the wrong item, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Item 34 of your report, Annex 3.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: October, November, the Od Sigurata Monastery. Can you please go back to the first book of the preliminary report and find insula 2. Insula 2, building 13. Is the date of the hit 6 December 1991, 1330 hours?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at item 35 of your report. October, November, the Franciscan Monastery. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at now -- look at the report of the institute now. That's insula 1.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: One.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just a minute. Insula 1-1. I thank my learned friend. In English it's 0060284.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The date of the hit is the 6th of December, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now please look at your report for October November, Antuninska Street number 11. Can you see it in your report for October and November, Antuninska Street number 11? It's item 36.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now kindly look at item 37 of your report. Does it indicate also 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, all buildings in Antuninska Street?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, please have a look at insula 3, institute report for October, November, December. Number 14. It's, in English, 0060378. The date of the hit is 6 December 1991, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now look at the page before that, one page before that, 0060377. It refers to Antuninska Street, number 24. Is the date of impact again the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now kindly ask you -- I don't know if you have the B/C/S version of the preliminary report before you. I don't think you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I would like the witness to have the B/C/S version, book 1, for the map which is only in the B/C/S version. Book 1. It's P51.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I should like you to have a look at the page which is marked 01069230. It's a map of insula number 3. 230 are the last digits. Will you please find it in the B/C/S version. 230.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Version the pages ending 229 and 230 are missing. We have two pages ending 228. They're the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe my learned friend can be of assistance, or maybe I should give you my copy, but then I will be left without anything to work with. That's my only copy. I'm sorry, do you have a copy by any chance?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please put this on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We also find that pages 231 and 232 are identical, so something appears to have gone wrong. I am in error there. There's a different note at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we proceed in this way? Is this convenient?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I should like you to look at -- first of all, tell me, are you familiar with this type of maps from your work with the preliminary report? Do you know how to look at these maps?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was familiar with these kinds of maps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right, then. Please look at the building which is indicated here with number 12, insula 3, building 12. Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, in the preliminary report itself, look at insula 3, building 12. Look at what building that is and then please tell the Chamber, which building is that, 3-12? Is it the building in Antuninska Street number 14? Insula 3-12, is it Antuninska 14?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what's written on the form, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, on the same side of the street with even numbers, do you see building number 13? The same street. Can you locate it on the map?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, please look at the preliminary report of the institute. That's insula 3-13. And tell me, is it Antuninska Street number 24?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The form number for Antuninska Street is number 4 -- 24.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see that between building 12 and building 13, according to the preliminary report of the institute, there is no damaged building in the period October, November, December 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the map, that would seem to be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that three buildings that you allegedly found in your report from October, November, 18, 20, and 22, are not referenced here?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wish that they actually had the street numbers on them. If those are indeed the buildings, though, I would say there was a reference. They're little dots on the facade of one of those buildings, and that would indicate damage to facade. But on the others there is no indication.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Which dots? Can you show us which dots? I can't see them.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. I think we're looking at different maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No. Please let us do it this way: First look at the map on the ELMO. Is there any indication on that map?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no indication of any damage on that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, do you have the following map ending with digits 231?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, you, Mr. Kaiser, look at the following map, map 231. Between buildings 12 and 13, can you see any dots indicated on the building which graphically reflects damage? Do you see any dots or any other marks?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I mentioned that I saw some dots that are on the street facade. The second building down, possibly the first building as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where, please? Could you place that page on the ELMO and show us so that we can see the dots too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the page 231 on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, show me on the building which corresponds to buildings 12 and 13. Where are the dots that indicate damage? That's building 13 that you are showing now, and the building down with two black triangles marked as 12. Where do you see black dots between 12 and 13?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I -- may I answer, please? If you see the street side here where the pointer is, it doesn't seem to come out very well on the viewer, but I can see them very, very clearly, and I can see them on the map. There is a series of one, two, three, four -- five, dots. There you see them. That would be damage to facades. You can -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In that case, what does this big round dot indicate, and what does it mean in the legend? Where are these little dots indicated in the legend that you claim are damage on the facade?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Second line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, if you look at the insula as a whole, look at building from 12 onwards, and tell me why that does not feature in the preliminary report, why none of these buildings have been identified in the preliminary report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't read the entries in the preliminary report, but if you say that none of this damage is described as facade damage, then I assume you're saying the truth, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is it true, then, that any building is indicated as damaged on the even side of the street between 12 and 14, in the street we are talking about? Sorry, between 14 and 24. In the records in the preliminary report, is there any trace of that, any trace of such damage?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. These would be numbers -- which numbers exactly? Because the numbers that they had -- they're different numbers on the maps and for houses here, which makes it a little bit confusing to follow. Okay. Which house numbers are these, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Eighteen, 20, and 22 are the house numbers.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no 18 here. I wish I could -- I'm sorry, could you repeat the numbers, sir, because I can't see the transcription.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: The house numbers are 18, 20, and 22.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Eighteen, 20, and 22; there are no forms here in this damage survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have my own copy of the map back.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a second, Your Honours. If you will bear with me for just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take your own report for October and November and look at item 13. Is it the Dedbelj [phoen] fortress?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let us recall, is that the fortress where the observation point of the Croatian army was located, observation post?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's where the observation post that I saw was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: I'd just like to ask if the "observation point of the Croatian army" was the phraseology of my learned friend. I don't think that came up in cross-examination at any point.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I accept this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that's the building; right?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the structure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you established that it was hit in October, November?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In book 1 of the institute's report. Look at reference Z30. It's 0061452. The date of the hit, is it the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now kindly look at Annex 2 of your report for October, November. Sorry, Annex 1. It's a map. It's a map where, at least at the top, it says the graphic depiction of damage inflicted during the shelling of the town in October, November, and December. So it's Prosecution Exhibit P62, tab 6, Annex 1.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's for the month of October, November on my map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Correct. Would you mind putting that map on the ELMO, please. Tell me first of all: Who drew up this map?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was drawn up by the members of the institute who did this particular survey.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you make this map a part of your report as an integral part of it?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I included this map for information to the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does this map correctly reflect what is contained in Annex 3 to your report?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not entirely correctly reflect what's in Annex 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where are the differences between Annex 3 and the map which you included in your report as Annex 1?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. We understand that this is the map they presented in Annex 3 is a different document which is based on the checking of the information that they gave us, including these locations that are on this map. There are some things which were unverifiable because they are dots in the water, and for us, dots in the water are not verifiable impacts. There are one or two that are perhaps missing, for example, down here. There would be one missing on the senior citizens' home. There are problems -- you can't see this very well, but in -- this is a bad reproduction of the map, but down here is the church of the Jesuits. There is a big bar, unfortunately, that comes down through there, and there were three dots on the church of the Jesuits. Now, the church of the Jesuits, as far as we could ascertain, was hit once, so there was a mixture between some fragments and direct impacts. They were all counted as one sort, the damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are a few things we didn't check in detail because we didn't have the time to check in detail, and these were basically along this part of the port.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, why did you include in your report which was prepared over a year after the events that we are discussing a map which is incorrect, which contains all these mistakes?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report wasn't prepared a year after the events. It was prepared at the beginning of January, a few weeks later. It was put in for information. It was very important to put in my annex, which unfortunately I didn't myself do a map. But the annex was stand for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to help me with this matter related to your report and the actual date when it was made. Perhaps I didn't see the date; I allow this as a possibility, as a mistake on my part. But please look at Exhibit 62, tab 6. Will you please be so kind as to find for me the date of your report. The only thing I can see about this report is this cover letter, 14th October 1993. Of course I allow for that being a possibility of that being an oversight on my part.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no date on it, but I can assure you that it was finished in early January 1992 and submitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you then tell me how come that an integral part of this report is also your letter, your introductory letter, which is dated 14th of October, 1993, if as you say you submitted the report in January 1992?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I really don't know what you're speaking about, sir. This may appear with other documents and there may be some confusion from that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: No, sir. I am referring to Prosecution Exhibit P62, tab 6, page 2 and 3 of the report, which is a letter. First, do you have the title page, the cover page, the title? Then follows this letter.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I understand, sir, this is document which is taken from the report on the battle of Dubrovnik and the law for done by the commission of experts in 1993. So you have a version of my report which has another document incorporated into it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to explain this for my benefit in great detail and very slowly, please, sir. What is contained in tab 6? That is your report; right? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This is the report which you prepared after returning from Dubrovnik, as you say; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in early January 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, please explain to me: What is the link between the introductory letter in that report, and what connection can this introductory letter have with your report to the commission of experts?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this is a letter that has been put into a copy of my report for the commission of experts. Dominik McAlea was the leader of the commission of experts team that was working in Dubrovnik, and all you have here is somebody has put in this particular letter regarding it as relevant to the work of the commission. I haven't seen this letter in a long time. I hope I can take a copy of it away. It has observations on my report. And it's dated 14th of October, 1993. And the mission of this particular team to Dubrovnik was at that time, sir, and I was part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But, sir, look at the content of that letter. Please tell me whether this letter makes a single reference to the report of the commission of experts by a single word. What it refers to is a report of the UNESCO monitors, observers. Perhaps I didn't read something properly in this mass of documents, but if I didn't, please be so kind as to indicate it for me.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained to you this is a letter written to, sent to the team leader, and it contains remarks on the report which I had made earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: A while ago, you told me that this letter had been written as part of the process of preparing the report of the commission of experts. What in this letter shows, demonstrates that letter is a part of that process?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: This contains -- I haven't read this in a long time, sir, but it contains my remarks about the original report of early January 1991, when I am sure that the commission was interested in knowing if I had any particular remarks to make about the earlier report that -- that could be useful for their work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If -- then --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the way, if I may interrupt you, it also indicates bombardments of May, June, 1992. I didn't write any reports about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: True; that is exactly why I'm asking you this. That is exactly why I'm asking you. How come that something which happened in May and June 1992 could have been incorporated into this whole story? And please, while we're at it, when you look at tab number 6, please explain to me this incorporation of it in this document. It is even labelled with ERN numbers 373, 374, 375, 376.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't label it. I don't really understand these kinds of questions. This is -- it would be very nice to have a complete copy of that report which is called the "Battle of Dubrovnik," I think, "and the Law of War," and to see how the whole document is laid out. This is not an introduction. This is an additional information for the use of the team of experts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can regale you by telling you that we will be coming to that particular document during my questioning, although to my great amazement and surprise, this document was not at all included in this batch of documents which has been presented to you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a report which this witness submitted to the United Nations Security Council, a very detailed report which has to do with events around Dubrovnik and which report in no way was mentioned here or given to you as part of the documents that have been presented here. So that the selective presentation of documents is something which has been repeated here. This is a key document. This is a report of a commission of experts which was actually the basis for the founding of this international tribunal. This witness who is before you was an active participant in this process, but until now you have been deprived of the possibility of seeing that report. I will seek to see to it that you are presented that report in -- as I continue my interrogation in the course of this day. And if the time is appropriate now, perhaps I could move that we take a break now, if you feel that that is convenient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. We'll have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic -- I'm sorry. Mr. Kaufman.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. Just two matters if I may, Your Honour, briefly. In the interval I was approached by the Victims and Witnesses Unit who requested me to bring to Your Honour's attention that the witness has now been on the stand for a fairly long time and he is growing slightly agitated that the cross-examination will be continuing for some time longer, if I can put it that way. Of course I don't want to interfere with Mr. Petrovic's discretion, what he feels is appropriate Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. for the defence of his client, but I thought it right and appropriate to bring it to Your Honours' attention so Your Honours are aware of this. That's the first matter. The second matter is one that I would wish to raise personally and it arises out of a comment that Mr. Petrovic made in the last question that was put to the witness before the interval. It was basically a comment that the Prosecution have selectively chosen exhibits to put before Your Honours. The Prosecution puts the exhibits which it feels are relevant to prove the indictment before Your Honours through this particular witness. There has been no hiding of evidence in this case, and insofar as that comment may be interpreted as suggesting that the Prosecution are withdrawing or hiding evidence from Your Honours, I would take objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, as to the first issue, the length of the cross-examination, are you in a position to give some indication of how much long your you will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is very difficult for me, Your Honours. Cooperation and cooperativeness implies two sides. If there were any cooperation on this particular matter, we would have finished this long ago, this story that we have been talking about for the last two days. But, Your Honour, I will do my very level best to finish today even if I have to give up some of my questions. But of course you will appreciate that I'm in no position to promise that. I will do my level best. But we have come to a situation whereby this report -- which is a key piece of documentation, which is the very basis of everything -- this is a report that you are acquainting yourselves with for the first time only now. Had you seen it before, I would not be in a position to have to point out the different aspects of the report now and to indicate the various things, the relevant issues, and I have to acquaint you now with when this report was given, how, and so on and so forth. I will do my level best for us to finish today the cross-examination, but despite the best wills, I cannot make that promise. I can only here repeat, I will try to do my best, Your Honours. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, we have been not raising the matter of time in respect of the evidence of this witness because we realise the importance of the report and Annex A to your case. And we realise from quite early in your cross-examination that the report cannot be taken at face value. You have made that very clear, and the resulting position is one which is very unsatisfactory, and I hope that discussions between counsel can overcome that situation in some way, failing which it will continue to be a difficulty for the cases of both the Prosecution and the Defence and for the Chamber itself later in the case. Nevertheless, having said all of that and given you to date unlimited time, I think you have made very considerable headway. And it ought to be possible now to focus your questions to a relatively speedy close to your cross-examination. If I could turn to the second matter. I don't call for any submissions, Mr. Petrovic. I would just observe that in the system and procedure of the Chamber, it is not the position that the Prosecution places every possible document or piece of evidence before the Chamber, although that may be an expectation in some other legal systems. It is the position that the Prosecution places before the Chamber the evidence which it thinks is relevant to the [sic] case, but it makes known to the Defence all other documents and evidence which is known to it which may be relevant to the Defence, so that it may be that you will want to introduce some documents or some evidence as part of your defence that the Prosecution have and have not used. That is a perfectly proper procedure for you to follow if it is relevant to your Defence. So I just make that observation, and I think we can just leave that issue where it lies. If you could proceed now with your cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you for all the comments which you have made. But in connection with the last thing which you said, I wish to say that the document which will soon be before you is not a document that I received from the Prosecution at any stage of the proceedings, but it is a Defence document. But let me not dwell on that; all in good time. But I am sure that you will for yourselves understand the significance of that document and how, generally speaking, is -- how selective, generally speaking, is the presentation of documents by the Prosecution. Sometimes these are public documents which we are in a position to obtain ourselves, but sometimes if something has not been disclosed to us either through the evidence of the Prosecution or the material under Rule 68 and knowing of this selective practice, this can indeed endanger the right of the accused, of the indictee, to a fair trial with all documentation being present whether it is of an exculpatory or incriminating nature, and that is what I was talking about, Your Honours. But of course I shall not belabour the point with any further argumentation but will move on to my specific questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Before you do, could I just note that I may have been careless in my use of language or there may have been an error in recording, but at line 24:16, I this meant to say relevant to its case. It is recorded as "relevant to the case." That correction will no doubt be made in due course. I'd be grateful. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before we move on to that report, Mr. Kaiser, are you able to continue? Do you agree that we continue?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a job, an employer, and an enormous amount of work on my desk. Let's continue and get finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I agree. Please look at this map on the ELMO which is Annex 1 to your report from an unspecified or, rather, unestablished year. Now, please look at it and show to the Chamber where the St. John Fortress is, if you're able to. And how many hits did it take? Can you count them? Five or six?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are eight hits or hits and fragment damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That is indicated on the map which is included in your report, which refers to October and November. Now, please look at the preliminary report, Z38. So Z38.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This, Your Honour, is 0068460.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So tell me, does this indicate a hit on the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the date which is indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And just another question in this regard, in respect of this map -- or, rather, two questions. I apologise. Look at the location of Pile. Do you know where that is? The Pile gates. Can you find in the preliminary report any references to Pile? There are four. I can say that right away to help you. Look first at Z27. That is the first reference to Pile. 0061449 is the number.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you see it? The date of the impact is the 6th of December. Do you agree that that is what it says, --

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- 6th of December? Now take a look at the Z36, 0061458. That is also the location of Vrata or Pile, the Pile gates. Does it also indicate that the hit was taken on the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please take a look then at the following document, the next page, 0061459, also the Pile gates. It states also that the hit was taken on the 6th of December, 1991. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And finally take a look at Z42, the approach bridge to Pile, 6 December 1991. Is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I submit to you that in the preliminary report there does not exist a single trace of any damage to the Pile gates and the surrounding parts of the ramparts which refers to any other date except to the 6th of December, whereas your report states that there were hits in October and November. Do you agree with this statement of mine?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to just look at my annex on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: There is no need for you to consult the annex. Please just tell me this: Do you agree that there is no other date referred to in the report except the 6th of December or -- or is there another date? This is what I'm interested in.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We no longer need the map. We are moving on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Did we get an answer to your question, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness said yes. I don't see it transcribed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I didn't hear it. I didn't --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The only damage mentioned in their preliminary report is for the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you please take a look at Annex 7 to your report. So please tell me -- Annex 7 to your report, if I may repeat, is P62, tab 6, Annex 7. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you first of all tell me where did you get this table?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. This -- this table was given to me by the institute when I went for the New Year's concert in Dubrovnik at the very end of 1991. I went there just for the concert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, what language is the table compiled?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's in French. I've very poor copy, but if I recall, I think it's in French.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How do you account for the fact that they gave you a table in the French language there? Where did they get this table when the report was never prepared in any other language except in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this was simply done in French locally. Mr. Carnez is Francophone, and he's not very, very anglophone at all. I think it was done out of consideration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, would it comes is a surprise to you that this table that you were given us a say on 31st of December, 1991, does not exist in the preliminary report of the 6th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen it in my cursory perusal of that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Does this surprise you? Do you have an explanation?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a little surprising that there would not be a table like this in that report.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you think it was an accidental omission?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know why it was omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you point it out to them at some point?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the course of your stay in Dubrovnik, did you draw up any other document, any -- anything else in writing with reference to this except for Annex 2, which is about ten words on one page?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a certain number of annexes which were drawn up because -- notably there was an annex which contained -- is a map, which was a map that we seen to the director general for his information, on the 8th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I was not precise enough in formulating my question. In your preparation of the methodology for the work to be done, did you draw up anything else, say for this document which contains only ten words? Did you make any other instruction, guideline, anything else?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember -- excuse me. I don't remember drawing up any other documents. This is for the institute, in other words.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Tell me, please, when did you leave Dubrovnik? I am referring to the period of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was 22nd of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And where did you go?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we -- we took the Krila Dubrovnika out and then we went to Italy.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did you spend the ten following days?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we went from Italy to Paris; Naples, Paris. And then I was in Paris up until the -- up until the trip for the midnight -- for the New Year's Eve concert at Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you kindly tell me this: Who invited you back to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this particular concert was organised by Minister Kouchner and also by UNESCO. And I was asked to accompany a high official of UNESCO, Mr. Lopez, who was the assistant director general for the bureau of external relations to Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did you arrive in Dubrovnik on the 31st of December, and when did you leave? At what time, if that was on the same day?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we arrived in the afternoon of the 31st. And then we -- in fact, we left at night. We went right back after New Year's to the port of Gruz and took the liner. It was a very short stay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who did you meet on that day? What did you do?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did meet the members of the institute. I spent most of my time with the UNESCO official, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he accompany you to those meetings at the institute?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lopez came to the institute.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was that an important event also for the people of the institute and the town of Dubrovnik, that a high official of UNESCO of your stature came to attend even for a brief stay this concert?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was still a consultant. It was very important for the director general to send a high official. This assured a better sort of representation, a more symbolic presence in the town. There was a lot of other visitors as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me why such an important thing as the visit of a representative of UNESCO and your own visit was something that you omitted to mention to the investigator who took your statement in November 2000, and January -- sorry, March 2001?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps he didn't ask questions in a complete way or ask about everything, and -- well, I just didn't -- I just didn't mention it, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: He asked you when you returned to Dubrovnik. Since you obviously answered one of his questions by saying, "I returned to Dubrovnik in November 1992 as part of the Council of Europe mission." Why didn't you tell him then what you are telling us today?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I guess at the time it didn't seem to me to be of enormous importance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Why does it seem important to you today when discussing the same subjects? The subject is still the same today and then.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I don't remember saying here that it was extremely important or relevant to the matter at hand.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that the visit of a high official of UNESCO was important, and you are somebody representing UNESCO, an escort of that high official.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but those are sort of separate matters. We were talking about war damage, and you're alluding to this visit. I'm not certain what the linkage is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It will be clear. Just tell me this: Did you continue your contacts with Nikola Obuljen after your first visit in November-December, and end December?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me if I continued my contacts -- at, in Dubrovnik during this short visit? Or later on?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the course of 1992, after the period we've just discussed.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the shellings of May and June 1992, I think I talked to him once on the phone. When I came to Dubrovnik in November 1992, I think I probably paid him a courtesy -- I paid him a courtesy visit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you talked to him once. Why him?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he spoke -- he spoke excellent English. He had been very -- rather friendly and I think he had appreciated what we'd tried to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What your statement given these years ago says is this; and three years ago you had a better recollection of the events than today. "Around May and June 1992 when the JNA again started to shell Dubrovnik, Bruno and I were in regular contact with Obuljen." Regular contact. Are you trying to hide today that you were in regular contact with him?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not trying to hide anything. If I made that statement back then, then it probably meant that I was in contact with him a few times on the phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how come that it -- that you were not in contact with your colleagues from the institute for the protection of monuments, architects, and others? Instead, you were in contact with the military commander of the town of Dubrovnik. Doesn't that seem odd to you? Was he in charge of contacts with you, the military commander?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I was in contact with the members of the institute by phone. I was more in contact with them. Secondly, I didn't -- I -- I didn't know that Mr. Obuljen was, in fact, a military commander because it was never, ever raised or brought to my attention. He was also -- he seemed to be a competent administrator as well. And Mr. Poljanic, I don't think Mr. Poljanic spoke very good English. So if I was going to have contact with somebody from the municipality, it would be somebody who was anglophone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But Mr. Kaiser, in the statement that you gave and signed, you don't say a word about being in contact with anyone else in 1992 save for Mr. Obuljen. You don't mention the people from the institute. You don't mention Poljanic. No one else. And you were not in contact with your colleagues or experts. You are in contact with the military commander. Even if you were not aware of his formal position, you knew when you saw six soldiers carrying weapons in the street, you call Obuljen. You don't call the institute or somebody else or one of your colleagues. How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in contact first. I don't understand why you -- you conclude that because it's not mentioned in the statement that I wasn't in contact with the colleagues. I was definitely in contact with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I draw that conclusion because in response to an obvious question by the ICTY Prosecutor -- investigator about your contacts in 1992, you answer: "Bruno and I were in contact with Obuljen." I suppose that otherwise you would have said, "We had contacts with Franic, colleagues, and people from the institute." But you mentioned only Obuljen, and you were very definitive about it; only Obuljen.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've given my answer to this question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you, Mr. Kaiser, play any role in the bringing of the indictment against Pavle Strugar?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really understand that question. How could I bring any -- how could I have any role in bringing the indictment against General Strugar?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Any role, I said. I didn't say you brought the indictment yourself. I asked if you had played any role in it. I didn't mean that you brought the indictment against him.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the basis of my mission and my mission report, that that is some sort of contribution to the indictment against General Strugar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From 1992 to year 2001, did you play any role in the provision of information contributing to the issuance of an indictment referring to -- related to Dubrovnik? Did you, in that period, have contacts with any -- with anyone employed by the OTP?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: If I may, before the witness answers the question. There are two questions in that particular question of my learned friend. One is: Did the witness have any role in providing information which contributed to the issuance of an indictment, which I would suggest is inviting a speculative answer. The witness cannot possibly know what went through the Prosecutor's mind when the indictment was submitted. The second part of that question, however, is a legitimate question. So I would ask for the Chamber to perhaps direct Mr. Petrovic to split his question up, and I would object to the first part of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question is better split, I agree, but I do Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. not agree that the first is speculative. You read more into it than is necessary, I think, Mr. Kaufman, and perhaps you might deal with the first part of it, Dr. Kaiser. Did you have any role? Did you take any step toward the issue of an indictment or toward persuading people to issue an indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was part of the mission of the commission of experts to Dubrovnik, and I was an expert on that mission. I also helped to work on the report. But if you regard that as working towards an indictment, well, I mean, I don't know what exactly the answer because I don't know what all the mechanisms were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That concluded effectively in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commission of experts' mission to Dubrovnik was -- yes. 1993. Otherwise, I can see no possible role that I would have taken or played.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Petrovic, has that dealt with the first part of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me. Accidentally or deliberately, the witness is confusing or mixing up things. Perhaps it's accidental. Look at what he says here. The commission of experts in Dubrovnik -- yes, yes, yes, Your Honour, but you are asking "was that concluded effectively in 1991." That was your question, Your Honour. And the witness replies, "Yes." And then he says, "1993." Your question was, "Was it concluded in 1991?" And he says, "Yes," and then, unless it's a mistake, he says "1993." That is line -- that is page 40, lines 5, 4 and 5, and your question is in line 2, page 40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I understood the witness to be correcting me. When I had said his role concluded in 1991, he was correcting me that the commission of experts' mission was later, in 1993. That's the way I understood him. But more importantly, the point he makes is that that is the only role he's played at all relevant to these proceedings. I think you were asking did he do something else, something different. And his answer to that is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to answer the second part of my question. Did you have any contacts with anyone from the Office of the Prosecutor in that period, from 1991 until 2001?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm trying to remember if I had any contact, because it seems that the interest of the Tribunal has been -- has been -- the Prosecutor's office has been a long one. I may have had some brief contact before 2001, but I really can't remember with whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, try to remember where these contacts took place.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I did come because I -- to the Tribunal -- because I was working as an expert witness on a number of other cases. And I met -- I could meet different people and for different teams and that sort of thing. But I can't remember if I met somebody or who I met. I may well have met somebody, but it would have been extremely informal contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you discuss events in Dubrovnik with anyone?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they -- if somebody asked me about Dubrovnik, I would have probably given my opinion or some -- I would have made some remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone ask you?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I thought I made it quite clear that I don't remember with whom -- if with whom -- with somebody, that I had contacts before that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you don't remember anything at all about it, any discussion of Dubrovnik within the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think I've answered the question. I don't remember this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anyone else ask you about events in Dubrovnik, about what was going on there? When I say "anyone else," I mean police authorities or maybe state authorities.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me about it. Nobody was very interested in my role.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, in your statement and in the examination-in-chief, why didn't you see fit to mention at any point that you took part in the commission that prepared a report for the UN Security Council specifically on the subject of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was basically answering questions. I assumed this would have been known by the Prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAUFMAN
utterances.text: And I can add in that particular context that I didn't feel it appropriate to ask the witness those questions. I think my learned friend knows that that's how the system works in the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course I do. But even though I know how the system works, I cannot conceal my astonishment at the fact that the report to the UN Security Council regarding Dubrovnik can be regarded by your party as irrelevant for this Trial Chamber. That's what I can't understand. Of course I understand the procedure. Now, tell me, please, who engaged you -- or, rather, first tell me, what kind of expert commission was it in which you took part that prepared the report for the UN Security Council?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the expert commission set up by the UN to pave the way for a tribunal, I think. This was a particular team that was sent out to look at the Dubrovnik area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that then a report of an expert commission to the UN Security Council under the UN Security Council Resolution number 780 from 1992?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that the UN Resolution which orders the establishment of a commission that would review any possible war crimes and suggest ways in which this institution that we are in today will be created? Is that the Resolution?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would sort of repeat myself. I assume that it is that Resolution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me who set up this commission.

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commission was set up under the aegis of the United Nations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is that the commission that was set up in keeping with the Resolution we are discussing?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, who engaged you to work on that commission?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm just trying to remember. I can't remember whether it came through UNESCO. I was -- I was approached. Perhaps by -- perhaps by Mr. Fenrick.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember?

utterances.speaker: COLIN KAISER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember the exact circumstances of my being engaged on it, but I remember Mr. Fenrick had a role. William Fenrick had a role in that commission.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who is Mr. William Fenrick?
